issues.legal_issue: The circumstances in which an accused may rely on the right of private defence to justify causing fatal harm.
material_facts: The accused claimed they used force to protect themselves and others after members of the other group had been injured, and some members of the accused group had also suffered injuries.
During the incident, the deceased came to support his injured family members and was struck on the head by the accused with wooden yokes.
The courts found that the accused had not established that the fatal force was necessary to ward off an attack or a continuing reasonable apprehension of danger.
issues.conclusion: The accused had not established that they were exercising the right of private defence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 96–106 of the Indian Penal Code, the right of private defence is defensive, arises when a reasonable apprehension of danger begins, and continues only while that apprehension lasts; it does not justify retaliation after the danger has passed. Under Section 105 of the Evidence Act, the accused bears the burden of establishing the plea, but need only show that it is more probable than not, and may do so through prosecution evidence. Injuries on the accused are relevant but do not automatically establish the defence; the circumstances must make the defensive response reasonable and necessary. The Court relied on Munshi Ram v. Delhi Administration, State of Gujarat v. Bai Fatima, State of U.P. v. Mohd. Musheer Khan, Mohinder Pal Jolly v. State of Punjab, Salim Zia v. State of U.P., Lakshmi Singh v. State of Bihar, Jai Dev v. State of Punjab, Biran Singh v. State of Bihar, Wassan Singh v. State of Punjab, Sekar alias Raja Sekharan v. State, Butta Singh v. State of Punjab, and Vidhya Singh v. State of M.P.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.accused_claimed_private_defence: The accused relied on the claim that the force used was to defend a person or property.
predicates.reasonable_probability_of_necessary_defe: The evidence makes it more probable than not that the force used was necessary to ward off an attack or a continuing reasonable apprehension of danger.

issues.definition: When an accused in an appeal from a criminal conviction claims private defence, the claim is not established if the evidence does not make it more probable than not that the force used was necessary to ward off danger.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a conviction for murder should be altered where the fatal injury resulted from a single blow in the circumstances of the incident.
material_facts: The accused struck the deceased on the head with a wooden yoke, and the record described the fatal injury as resulting from a single blow.
The Court considered that the blow was delivered with a small, light wooden yoke and assessed it in the context of the incident as a whole.
The accused had been convicted of murder, and the Court had rejected their claim of private defence.
issues.conclusion: The conviction was altered from murder to culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Part I, and a custodial sentence of ten years was imposed.
issues.legal_principle: A single blow resulting in death does not invariably exclude murder; the circumstances of each case must be assessed. On the facts here, the Court altered the conviction under Section 302 to Section 304 Part I of the Indian Penal Code.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction and single_fatal_head_blow and blow_delivered_with_small_light_weapon and circumstances_considered_as_a_whole_support_reduced_offence

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for murder.
predicates.single_fatal_head_blow: The death resulted from a single blow to the head.
predicates.blow_delivered_with_small_light_weapon: The blow was delivered with a small, light weapon.
predicates.circumstances_considered_as_a_whole_supp: The circumstances of the incident, considered as a whole, support treating the offence as culpable homicide rather than murder.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a murder conviction, a single fatal head blow with a small, light weapon supports altering the conviction to culpable homicide when the circumstances as a whole support that reduced offence.
